newsitem.title: ISRAEL: No credit for Israeli bridegrooms, rabbi says.
newsitem.headline: No credit for Israeli bridegrooms, rabbi says.

text.p: Israel's chief rabbi has warned Jewish bridegrooms against buying wedding rings with credit cards, the Itim news agency said on Monday.
Chief Rabbi Mordechai Eliahu told Itim a couple in northern Israel almost had to remarry after it transpired a credit card company had failed to bill the husband for a ring before the ceremony.
Under Jewish ritual law, a bridegroom's marriage vow -- made as he slips the ring on the finger of his bride -- is valid only if he has legal ownership of the ornament.

Mordechai ruled the marriage was valid because the payment delay was the credit company's fault, but warned bridegrooms not to buy wedding rings with a credit card unless it was clear the debt would be paid before the ceremony, Itim said.
